newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Vodacom bullish on mobile phone prospects.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Vodacom bullish on mobile phone prospects.

text.p: South Africa's Vodacom said on Tuesday that the country's already booming mobile phone sector was set for more fast-paced growth.

Vodacom has more than 640,000 subscribers, giving it about 60 percent of the South African market. The industry, which is barely three years old, has attracted more than a million mobile phones users.

"Our initial growth projections catered for 250,000 subscribers within 10 years. We now expect to exceed one million by the year 1999," Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig told a news conference.
Vodacom is owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc, Rembrandt Group Ltd and Telkom. South Africa's second operator, MTN, is owned by Cable & Wireless Plc and several local groups including M-Cell Ltd.
Knott-Craig was speaking at a presentation on Vodacom's early fulfillment of various licence criteria involving projects aimed at creating wealth in post-apartheid South Africa.
In the next decade Knott-Craig said he expected the industry to make more strides forward, possibly overtaking the number of fixed telephones in the country.
"The number of cellular phones in South Africa will easily exceed four million and probably approach 10 million," he said.

Sub-Saharan Africa is notoriously underserved by telephones and so offers a money-spinning opportunity to mobile networks. The continent of 700 million people has just 12 million phones -- less than on New York's Manhattan Island.

Four million of the continent's phones lie in South Africa and Post, Telecommunications and Broadcasting minister Jay Naidoo said cooperation between mobile operators and government would see South Africa position itself as a communications hub.
"It is through this cooperation that we will be able to catapult our entire country into the next century and establish our country as an important hub of communications," he said.
